title: UtilityWeights
description: Data file content/behaviour/utility.json: how the routine layer (utility AI, fallback when no AI answer is there) scores the options the core offers. A score is weight x curve(need value) x belief factor; curves are point tables with linear interpolation (no transcendental math in the core). Placeholders until Marcel decides.

distance_falloff.description: Score factor lost at the edge of the perception radius (linear with distance; 0 = distance does not matter).

learning_step.description: Confidence added per experience (frame for learning; B4a extends it).

unknown_target_belief.description: Belief factor for a target whose property the inhabitant does not know yet (trying unknown things).

search_weight.description: Score factor of looking further away (search_action) against a target in sight: the search scores urgency x the surest helpful belief x this value, so a weak or doubtful target in sight still competes. At most unknown_target_belief (checked at load): trying something unknown close by never loses to searching far away.

search_give_up_hours.description: Game hours after which an inhabitant stops looking further away for a need, until the need is met or something believed helpful is in sight again (no endless search for what is gone or was heard wrongly).

RuntimeNeedConsideration.description: How the routine weighs a need an invention brought (A1372, TL B2658): the need's urgency (weight x curve of its value) for using a thing of the invention's type in sight with the need's first action that has timing. Only things in sight, no search. Omitted = the routine never seeks such a need.

curve.description: Points [x, y] with ascending x in 0..1.

yields_to_needs.description: The score yields to pressing needs, as for a consideration.

RepetitionLimit.description: Ends repeating without effect (W1696): when an inhabitant does the same action on the same target at about the same spot this many times in a row and none of them changed a need, mood, belief or relation by at least min_effect, the action rests for a while; it is neither chosen nor offered to the decider, and an answer still waiting for it is dropped. Optional: without it nothing rests.

max_repeats_without_effect.description: Repeats in a row without any effect after which the action rests.

rest_hours.description: Game hours the action then rests (cooldown).

same_place_m.description: Distance in metres from where the run began within which a repeat counts as the same spot.

min_effect.description: Smallest change of a need, mood or the will to live that counts as an effect; less (e.g. topping up a need that is nearly full) counts as nothing.

exempt_actions.description: Actions that never rest (doing nothing, e.g. idle): resting them would only send the inhabitant off on strolls away from water and food; their calm look is the presentation's task (pose_cadence).

InhabitantTarget.description: Which other inhabitants a consideration aims at.

relation.description: familiar = the inhabitant's own relationship to the other reaches togetherness.min_trust and togetherness.min_affection of the inhabitant model (the one definition of familiar; start values count while no relationship is kept), and the other is not asleep by togetherness.sleep_action. Needs the togetherness section (checked at load).

Consideration.description: Scores an action. With target_property the core offers the action on every perceived object; the belief that the object has that property scales the score. With target_inhabitant it offers the action on other inhabitants in sight instead.

avoid_properties.description: Properties that make the option worse when the inhabitant believes the target has them (factor 1 - confidence each), e.g. salty for drinking.

search_action.description: Action without a target (vocabulary target none) for looking further away while the inhabitant believes some kind of thing has target_property and nothing it avoids; scored with search_weight. With target_inhabitant: while the inhabitant knows someone of that relation and none of them is in sight (a sleeper in sight counts as there: nobody walks off from a sleeping partner); scored urgency x search_weight. Needs a target_property or a target_inhabitant. Absent or null = the need waits until something turns up.

target_inhabitant.description: Another inhabitant as the target (W1744): the action (vocabulary target inhabitant) is offered on every other inhabitant in sight that the inhabitant has met, that stands in this relation to it and that is not asleep, scored urgency x the distance factor (distance_falloff). The inhabitant acts on its own relationships only. Needs target_property null, no avoid_properties and no novelty_curve. Absent or null = no inhabitant target.

need.description: Need whose value is the curve input; null = constant input 1.

trait.description: Character trait whose value (0..1) scales the score, e.g. curiosity. Absent or null = no trait.

yields_to_needs.description: The score yields to pressing needs, as exploring with a novelty_curve does (B2-6 R14): scaled by 1 - the highest urgency of the needs that can be neglected, and 0 while one is below its neglect threshold. Absent or false = no scaling.

novelty_curve.description: Exploring (TL #19921): the action is offered on every perceived object, scaled by this curve over the novelty of the object's type (1 - the inhabitant's surest belief about it; 1 = knows nothing). It yields to pressing needs: scaled by 1 - the highest urgency of the needs that can be neglected, and 0 while one is below its neglect threshold. Needs target_property and search_action null. Absent or null = no exploring.

curve.description: Points [x, y] with ascending x in 0..1.
